text:
lia: Morning — Borealis Bank kickoff in 2pm. They want a short POC (72h) to prove migration from CompetitorY. Primary asks: function/tool-call parity, token-cost delta, answers to their security questionnaire (SAML/SCIM, VPC peering, BYO-KMS), and a demo SLA for p50/p99. cc @omar @devin @emma
omar: I can spin up a small adapter. CompetitorY often emits inline actions like [EXEC:pull_customer id=123]. Plan is prefix-detect and map to structured tool invocations. Quick prototype available by EOD.
devin: I'll run a 300-prompt diff set (mix of short chat, long instruction, and tool-heavy prompts). Running two configs: temp=0.0 + our default sampling. Will output token deltas, latency distribution, and a normalized response diff. ETA first pass in ~6h.
security-bot: Security questionnaire created: https://redwood.example.com/secforms/borealis-2026. Checklist: SOC2, ISO27001, SAML, VPC, customer-managed KMS, audit-log retention (>=90d).
lia: Pricing: can we give them a short Dedicated trial vs hosted pricing so they can compare unit economics? Need numbers to show during presales call.
emma: Quick slide numbers: hosted generation $0.018/1k tokens, embeddings $0.0035/1k. Rough Dedicated estimate: ~$9k/mo for a 2-node reserve with their target latency. I'll pull formal quote from finance by EOD.
omar: Adapter mapping example (prototype): ```json
{
  "pattern": "^\\[EXEC:(.*?)\\]",
  "map": "extract name+args -> {\"name\":name,\"args\":parsed_args}"
}
``` We'll also normalize stop sequences and trailing whitespace to reduce diffs.
devin: Early diff summary (first 50 prompts): ~9% token variance when using default sampling; forcing stop tokens and temp=0.0 drops variance to ~2.5%. Tool-call normalization reduces false tool-detection by ~70%. I will publish full CSV + example parses shortly.
patrick: Legal/enterprise blocker: they insist on a data residency clause and right-to-audit. Also need explicit KMS handling in contract (BYO-KMS). I'll engage legal. Expect 48-72h for contract language.
ops-oncall: We can provision VPC peering. Need approved CIDR ranges and billing code. Turnaround ~24h after info.
lia: Owners: adapter=omar, diff+reports=devin, pricing=emma, security/legal=patrick, infra peering=ops-oncall. I'll compile a POC checklist and share link post-kickoff.
emma: Also confirm billing granularity question: Borealis asked per-token vs per-request pricing and minimum monthly commit thresholds. I'll include both in the quote.
devin: Note on tests: include corner-case prompts that trigger multi-tool sequences and stop-token edge cases. Those tend to drive the largest response deltas.
lia: Good call. @devin please include 25 tool-heavy prompts in the set.
devin: Added. First full diff will be uploaded to the POC folder: https://redwood.example.com/pocs/borealis-1739/diffs
patrick: Legal looped in. I'll post status in this thread when we have contract language.
lia: Thanks everyone — reconvene after devin posts results. Quick ask for the POC deck: include one before/after mapping example showing original inline action -> normalized tool call.
ops-oncall: Ack. Ping me with the IPs when ready.
lia: :white_check_mark:
